ROLL CALL: At 6:03 p.m., on Monday, March 25, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Police Chief Kennedy, Fire Chief
Ragusa

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PRESENTATIONS

1.  ANNUAL BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS APPOINTMENTS – F2M24-37

  City Clerk MYLES delivered a staff report. The terms of office for all members of the City’s
  various Boards and Commission expired on March 25, 2024; therefore, it was appropriate for
  Councilpersons to appoint or reappoint their representatives at this time. With the exception of
  the Youth Commission, each representative may serve for a maximum of eight consecutive
  terms of one year each. Appointments would be effective for a period commencing March 25,
  2024 and ending March 24, 2025.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER appointed Je-Show Yang to the
  Environmental Sustainability Commission and Dylan Littlefield to the Historic Preservation
  Commission. Councilmember LEE appointed Melissa Michelson to the Historic Preservation
  Commission. Councilmember MALONEY appointed Elliott Lee to the Transportation
  Commission. Vice Mayor PÉREZ stated that she planned numerous appointees and that
  therefore she would provide a list to City Clerk Myles at a later date. Mayor MAZA stated that
  he did not have finalized list of appointees at this time, but would provide a list to Ms. Myles at
  a later date.

3-25-24  1
   Action Taken:  Councilmembers announced their new appointments to Environmental
  Sustainability Commission, Historic Preservation Commission, and Transportation
  Commission, with each appointment to be effective for a period commencing March 25, 2024

2.  ALHAMBRA COMMUNITY CENTER DESIGN UPDATE – F2M22-65, M2M24-51

  Director of Parks and Recreation MACIAS delivered a staff report and a presentation, which
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office. On November 13, 2023, the City Council provided staff
  direction to pursue the “Around the Campfire” building design rendering for the purpose of
  completing the Environmental Impact Report (EIR) project description. In order to fall within
  the $25 million dollar project budget, the proposed size of the community center must be
  reduced to 17,000 square feet. Given the budget input and an adaptive re-use request from
  the Alhambra Historical Society, the team produced four modified design solutions for a 17,000
  square foot community center (two 100% new build, and two adaptively reusing a portion of
  the existing structure). The design team also provided designs with the option to expand their
  square footage by approximately 4,000 square feet should there be additional funding in the
  future. Staff l presented four options. The four designs included Scheme I. “Around the Camp
  Fire”, Scheme 2. “Overlooks,” Alternative I. “Flowscapes,” and Alternative II, “Connecting
  Gems.” Tarrah BEEBE, an architect from consultant KFA, made additional presentation of the
  designs. She outlined the differences between the new construction options and the
  preservation options.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked State Senator Susan Rubio
  and Assemblymember Mike Fong for their contributions to the community center project. She
  also thanked the speakers and referred to comments regarding the need for inclusivity and
  the need for safe student spaces. She expressed that the community center would continue
  to provide multiple levels of programming for residents. She spoke about the compromises
  made and the desire to preserve elements of the original building. She further discussed the
  need to continue the history of Alhambra. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER supported Alternative 2
  “Connecting Gems.”

  Councilmember LEE expressed that this was a difficult decision and spoke regarding the
  points raised by public speakers. She compared and contrasted Scheme 2 “Overlooks” and
  Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems, and discussed the plans with Ms. BEEBE. Ms. BEEBE
  answered questions. Ms. LEE discussed the merits of preserving the original building in terms
  of the neighborhood and supported Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems.”

  Councilmember MALONEY thanked the public for their input as well as the work of the
  consultants and staff. He discussed the background of the project. He went on to compare
  and contrast Scheme 2 “Overlooks” and Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems.” He expressed
  preference for Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems” due to the open space provided. He continued
  to discuss the merits of an open space and the benefits of a new community center space. He
  discussed the safety issues regarding asbestos abatement, the CEQA process, and seismic
  upgrades with City Attorney MONTES. Mr. MONTES and Mr. Chuck COWLEY, from the City’s
  consultant, Cowley Corbis, responded to questions. Mr. MALONEY discussed benign neglect
  of other historic buildings in Los Angeles and the renewed interest in preserving historical
  structures. He further supported Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems.”

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ thanked the public for their comment and referred to comments made
  regarding inclusivity and equity. She spoke regarding the changes to designs due to project
  costs. Ms. PÉREZ and Ms. BEEBE discussed differences between Scheme 2 “Overlooks” and
  Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems” with regards to programming spaces. Ms. PÉREZ, Ms.
  BEEBE and City Manager BINNQUIST further discussed funding sources and grant
  opportunities for the project. Ms. PÉREZ went on to discuss the potential use of nearby
  greenspace, historic preservation, adaptive reuse, and connecting to the history of Alhambra.
  She also thanked State Senator Rubio and Assemblymember Fong.

  Mr. MALONEY went on to discuss grant opportunities and expressed disappointment
  regarding the reduced square footage due to project costs. He continued to discuss the city’s
  pursuit of grant funding. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. MONTES discussed alternative designs
  should additional funds get awarded, and the impact of design changes during the CEQA
  process. Ms. PÉREZ, Mr. MONTES, Mr. COWLEY, and Mr. MALONEY continued to discuss
  the project, CEQA and adaptive reuse designs which could incorporate larger space.

  Mayor MAZA also thanked Senator Rubio and Assemblymember Fong for their contributions,
  staff, consultants, the public, and the Alhambra Historical Society. He stated that he supported
  historic preservation and that there was a tremendous opportunity to produce a project in its
  best and most efficient form for residents as well as a building that would outlive Council. He
  commented on his background as a realtor and his involvement in designing new constructions
  that blend in an architecturally historic neighborhood. He discussed the limitations of

  4
3-25-24
   preservation such as overall square footage, ceiling height, and room size; and that it was not
  providing the most efficient use of the building. He supported Scheme 2 “Overlooks,” and
  highlighted the ways in which parts of the original building could be incorporated into a legacy
  building. He went on to speak to the limitations of the Joslyn Center in terms of programming.
  He stated that he would like to work with the Historical Society to preserve and incorporate
  elements and he added that the design of a new construction could match the aesthetics of
  the neighborhood. He expressed that in order to be fully responsible to the whole community,
  that the City needed to produce the best form possible for a building which would have inviting
  spaces to seniors and youth. He continued to discuss possible methods for preserving
  elements of the original building in a new construction.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the Mayor for his work on the subcommittee and working
  with the community in terms of preservation, however she expressed preference for Alternative
  2 “Connecting Gems” in order to preserve as much of the original building as possible. She
  made a motion to select Community Center building design option Alternative 2 “Connecting
  Gems,” to complete the EIR project description. Ms. LEE seconded her motion. Mr. MONTES
  made clarifications regarding the motion, the project timeline as it related to the EIR project
  description, the architectural design request for proposal process, and requested that the
  description proposal include language allowing for additional square footage should grant
  funding become available in the near future. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER accepted the
  amendment to her motion. Mr. MAZA stated that while he still fully supported Scheme 2
  “Overlooks,” he accepted Alternative 2 “Connecting Gems” as a second option.

  Action Taken:  City Council provided staff direction and chose Community Center
  building design option, “Connecting Gems,” for completing the Environmental Impact Report
  (EIR) project description, including language allowing for additional square footage should
  grant funding become available in the near future; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-51)

3.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALHAMBRA PARK BANDSHELL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
  –F2M24-22, N2M24-18, C2M24-19, M2M24-49

  On February 12, 2024, the City Council approved a Notice Inviting Bids (NIB) for the Alhambra
  Park Bandshell Project. On Thursday, March 14, 2024, the City Clerk received three bids for
  the Project. The bids ranged from $85,000.00 (Sanz Construction, Inc.) to $178,360.00
  (Newbuild Construction and Restoration, Inc.). State law requires all contractors and sub-
  contractors be registered with the Department of Industrial Relations (DIR). Also, the NIB
  required proof of DIR registration upon submittal, however, State law does not require that a
  bid include the submittal of proof of DIR registration. Sanz Construction, Inc, did not provide
  proof of DIR registration with its bid submittal, but staff was able to verify the company’s status
  on the DIR website. Staff recommended that the proof of DIR registration submittal is waived
  and Sanz Construction, Inc., be awarded the contract based on the lowest responsive bid.

  Discussion:  None.

   Action Taken:  City Council awarded contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Sanz Construction Inc in the amount of $85,000.00 for
  the Alhambra Park Bandshell Project; determined the project is exempt from CEQA pursuant
  to CEQA guidelines section 15301; waived the requirement for proof of DIR registration with
  the bid submittal; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M24-49)

4.  RESOLUTION OPPOSING INITIATIVE NO. 21-0042A1, THE TAXPAYER PROTECTION
  AND GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY ACT – F2M24-19, R2M24-10

  On January 4, 2022, the California Business Roundtable filed the “Taxpayer Protection and
  Government Accountability Act” (Initiative No. 21-0042A1). On February 1, 2023, the measure
  qualified for the November 2024 ballot. If passed, the Taxpayer Protection and Government
  Accountability Act would amend the California Constitution with provisions that limit voters'
  authority and input, adopt new and stricter rules including 2/3 voter approval for raising taxes
  and fees, and make it more difficult to impose fines and penalties for violating state and local
  laws. The measure would have significant negative impacts on local government operations
  and core service delivery, and would put valuable local government tax and fee revenues at
  risk statewide. The proposed constitutional initiative was sponsored by the California Business
  Roundtable.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-10 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra opposing Initiative 21-0042A1, the Taxpayer
  Protection and Government Accountability Act; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, PÉREZ, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA

5.  RESOLUTION SUPPORTING A PEACEFUL RESOLUTION TO THE ONGOING CONFLICT
  AND HUMANITARIAN CRISIS IMPACTING GAZA AND ISRAEL – F2M24-16, R2M24-9

  On January 22, 2024, Mayor Maza and the City Council discussed support for peace in the
  Middle East related to the ongoing conflict and humanitarian crisis. Following that meeting, on
  February 12, 2024, Mayor Maza sent a letter to Congresswoman Judy Chu, with copies to
  Senator Durazo and Assemblymember Mike Fong, encouraging Federal support for peace, a
  lasting cease-fire and the safe return of all hostages in Gaza and Israel. In addition, on
  February 12, 2024, the Council requested a Resolution in support of peace be drafted for a
  subsequent City Council meeting.

6.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR PA&ED
  FOR THE FREMONT INTERCHANGE PROJECT UNDER THE 710 MOBILITY
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS – F2M19-32, C2M20-43, M2M24-50

  On April 10, 2020, the City Council awarded a contract to Kimley-Horn for the professional
  engineering services to advance the 710 concepts. The firm’s contract was for three-years
  expiring on August 26, 2023, with an option to extend the contract two years, depending on
  the needs of the project(s) and contractor performance. On August 28, 2023, staff
  recommended approval to amend the contract with Kimley Horn for a longer term through
  August 2025 and for additional project management to further study key project components,
  including the relationship of the project to the business, residential, and school communities,
  and the need for expanded outreach and technical support to the City. Work under the
  proposed Second Amendment with Kimley Horn specifically included: Project Management;
  Research and Data Collection; Surveying and Mapping; Traffic Operations Report;
  Environmental Study and Documentation; Project Report; and Public Outreach and
  Engagement. The final Project Approval/Environmental Document (PA&ED) tasks were
  expected to be completed by the end of 2026; consequently, staff also recommended the
  contract with Kimley Horn be amended through December 31, 2026. The total costs under
  Amendment 2 were $4,236,525.79.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Second Amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and the City Attorney, to the contract with Kimley-Horn (C2M20-
  43) for professional engineering consulting services for PA&ED for the Fremont Interchange
  Project at a cost of $4,236,525,79; extended the contract with Kimley Horn through December
  31, 2026; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.
  (M2M24-50)
